title: Serbian elections on Italian Wikipedia: from an editathon to a workshop
content:
The significance of the 2026 parliamentary elections in Serbia has extended beyond the borders of this Balkan country, becoming a topic of debate throughout Europe and beyond. Often, however, this has taken place without the minimum foundations required to do so productively.

To quote Luigi Einaudi, the second President of the Italian Republic, one must ‘first understand, then discuss, then decide’. Wikipedia still plays a vital role today in providing accurate political information, offering a source that aims for the greatest possible neutrality, rejecting both the political partisanship of many media outlets – often amplified by social media – and the complacent partisanship of artificial intelligence, where there is no fundamental truth but rather one that varies according to each user’s preferences.

Wikipedia, in fact, is the same for everyone, regardless of political orientation: there is no right-wing Wikipedia nor a left-wing Wikipedia; if someone has a problem with the facts and is unable to provide sources to back up their claims, that is their own problem!

title: Attiéké, Abodan and a Whole Lot of Open Knowledge: My WikiIndaba Reflections
content:
Some discoveries happen in conference rooms, others happen over a plate of food or during a cultural performance. At WikiIndaba, I had my fair share of all three.

Did you know that the traditional skills involved in making Attiéké are recognised by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity? And that the dance I initially thought was Adowa was actually Abodan? What an epiphany!

These were just two of the many things I discovered at WikiIndaba. Beyond the sessions, presentations and conversations, the conference offered an opportunity to learn about other cultures, reflect on the work we do as Wikimedians and, importantly, think about where our movement is headed.

As we celebrate 25 years of the Wikimedia movement, I left with several thoughts about knowledge equity, African languages, community development and how we can make the knowledge we create more visible and accessible.

Here are a few reflections that stayed with me.

title: Turkmen Wikipedia: The Quiet, Resilient Corner of the Free Encyclopedia
content:
Every language edition of Wikipedia has its own heartbeat. Some move at breakneck speed, shaped by thousands of daily contributors, sprawling WikiProjects, and automated bots. Others grow slowly, steadily, and quietly-held together by a small circle of dedicated volunteers who care deeply about seeing their language represented in the world’s largest free knowledge repository.

Turkmen Wikipedia (tk.wikipedia.org) belongs to that second group.

At first glance, a smaller Wikipedia can look understated compared to larger regional neighbors like Russian, Turkish, or Uzbek Wikipedias. Yet behind the modest article counts and quieter Recent Changes feed lies a remarkably resilient project-one where every well-sourced paragraph, every standardized template, and every newly created article carries outsized meaning for readers searching in Turkmen.

According to Meta-Wiki’s List of Wikipedias, Turkmen Wikipedia sits around 200th place among all active language editions-a compact, steadily maintained project with deep room to grow

title: Documenting Uzbekistan Through Wikimedia Commons: My Journey as a Contributor
content:
Wikimedia Commons plays an important role in preserving and sharing freely licensed photographs,videos and other media with people around the world. For me, it has also become a way to document Uzbekistan, Uzbek people, sporting achievements and everyday life.

I began contributing to Wikimedia Commons in October 2014. Over the years my interests and activities have developed, but one objective has remained important: making useful visual material about Uzbekistan more accessible to everyone.

As of November 2026, I have uploaded 1,424 files to Wikimedia Commons.

One of my main areas of interest is Uzbek football. Football is an important part of the country’s sporting and cultural life; yet many Uzbek footballers, clubs, stadiums and sporting events remain under represented in freely accessible visual collections.

Through my contributions, I have tried to help fill this gap.

My uploads include photographs of Uzbek footballers, teams, stadiums and football-related events.

I have also contributed photographs of stadiums and teams from different levels of Uzbek football.

title: SICSS Ouagadougou 2026: When Wikimedia Meets Computational Social Sciences in Francophone Africa
content:
From August 10 to 21, 2026, Ouagadougou, the capital of Burkina Faso, hosted the second edition of the Summer School in Computational Social Sciences (SICSS). Two days were devoted to Wikipedia, Wikidata, and open data, which were presented not only as platforms for contributing to content creation but also as sources of structured data for the study, analysis, and understanding of society.

What happens when researchers think of Wikipedia and Wikidata not only as sources of knowledge, but also as data that can help us better understand society ?

It was precisely this question that guided Wikimedia’s activities during the Summer Institute in Computational Social Sciences (SICSS 2026). SICSS is an international network of summer schools dedicated to computational methods in the social sciences. The 2026 session took place from August 10 to 21 at the Higher Institute of Population Sciences (ISSP) at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. It was made possible thanks to the support of Wiki In Africa, funded by the Wikimedia Foundation’s research fund.

title: Wikimedia Foundation Bulletin 2026 Issue 22
content:
Here is a quick overview of highlights from the Wikimedia Foundation since our last issue on November 6. Previous editions of this bulletin are on Meta. Let foundationbulletin@wikimedia.org know if you have any feedback or suggestions for improvement!

  • Thinking Beyond Pageviews: Traffic to Wikimedia sites is changing reflecting a rapidly changing internet ecosystem. We dig in deep to the pageview data to understand more thoroughly what is changing and how.
  • A place called “Home”: Home is designed to be a central place for Wikipedians at every stage, to find meaningful ways to participate and grow, through suggested edits (with a new task selection process), mentorship and impact. It was released as a Beta feature to 9 Wikipedias and will replace Special:Homepage at most of these wikis.
  • Collaborative embroidery Wikimania 2027: Submit a fabric square with your message about “The Internet we want”, which will be stitched into a larger tapestry inspired by the Chilean tradition of arpilleras. Find out how to participate in this historic Wikimedia movement-wide art project, regardless of whether you are traveling to Santiago in person.

title: From Botswana to Côte d’Ivoire: My First Wiki Indaba Experience as an AffCom Advisor
content:
From 13–15 November 2026, I had the incredible opportunity to attend my first Wiki Indaba Conference in Côte d’Ivoire. It was a memorable experience filled with learning, meaningful conversations, new connections and opportunities to contribute to discussions shaping the future of the Wikimedia movement in Africa.

The conference, organised by Wikimedia Community User Group Côte d’Ivoire, was held under the theme “Africa’s Future: Knowledge Equity and Innovation.” It brought together Wikimedians from across Africa and the diaspora to exchange ideas, share experiences and explore ways of strengthening free knowledge on the continent.

For me, this experience was particularly special because I participated in different capacities: as an Advisor to the Wikimedia Affiliations Committee (AffCom), alongside fellow members of Wikimedia Community User Group Botswana, and as an Africa Baraza representative.

The conference opened with welcoming remarks, followed by an inspiring keynote address from Anusha Alikhan, Chief Communications Officer at the Wikimedia Foundation.

title: Wikidata Reference Validator Tool: Improving Verifiability Across Wikidata
content: Wikidata depends on reliable, verifiable references to maintain trust across its open knowledge base. During the Wiki Indaba 2026 Hackathon, our team worked on Project 04 under the Verification and Consistency track, mentored by Josef Anthony and Birusha. Together, we updated the Wikidata Reference Validator Tool, a dedicated utility designed to check references, identify broken links, and help editors maintain the reliability and verifiability of information on Wikidata. The core issue our team set out to tackle is the presence of broken or outdated external references on Wikidata. While some references remain fully accessible and work correctly, others are completely broken because the links no longer work and return 404 errors. Another major challenge comes from outdated links, where a page still exists online but contains old or no longer maintained information. These broken and outdated references undermine the reliability of the platform by making it much harder to verify information, which is why identifying them automatically is critical to improving Wikidata verifiability.

title: Picking up the mic: A speaker’s experience from Wiki Indaba 2026
content:
In my mind I was preparing for an unexpected turn, as this was my first conference with Wikimedia. I got a scholarship to attend the 2026 Wiki Indaba and my plan was to just be a part of the audience through every session within the three days. That changed as I got a last-minute invitation to step in for a colleague from the Wikimedia Kenya User Group who had proposed a lightning talk that got approved but was unable to secure a scholarship to travel.

The lightning talk on growing Swahili Wikipedia: the lessons from Kenya’s translation model happened on the third day of the conference.

The lightning talk was based on a common challenge faced by different indigenous African languages in scaling their editions of Wikipedia: ‘How do we scale digital knowledge in under-represented languages without overwhelming new editors?’

What we realized back in Kenya is that one of the biggest hurdles wasn’t a lack of language fluency or enthusiasm but the belief that Wikimedia tools were too technical. To test this, we trained over thirty volunteers on using the translation tool for Swahili content. We walked them through using the content translation tool and paired them with experienced peers.

title: Scoring a Goal for Free Knowledge: How WikiSport’s Football Project Transformed Uzbek Football Coverage on Wikipedia
content:
In Uzbekistan, football isn’t just a pastime–it’s a national obsession. Yet for years, fans searching for reliable, structured information in Uzbek about their own domestic leagues, historic clubs, or local players often hit a dead end. Articles on the Uzbek Wikipedia were either missing entirely or consisted of little more than a single stub sentence.

Launched as a specialized thematic track under the broader WikiStipendiya marathon, the WikiSport: Football project set out to change that. Open to contributors of all backgrounds regardless of where they live, the initiative combined grassroots community editing with institutional sports partnerships to build an encyclopedic archive of Uzbek football from the ground up.

Rather than relying solely on scattered online summaries, editors used these connections and authoritative sports journalism to systematically document decades of post-independence football history-turning the project page into both a coordination hub and a living index of Uzbek football knowledge.

title: Women Wiki camp in Southeast Serbia
content:
Between April and October 2026, Wikimedia Serbia ran Digital Voices of Southeast Serbia, a project supported by the CIVICUS Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI), aimed at closing both the gender and regional knowledge gaps on Wikipedia. By combining local research with an in-person mentorship camp in Pirot, the project helped women from southeastern Serbia overcome the fear of online judgment and publish 41 new articles on Serbian Wikipedia, with two participants now stepping up to lead their own Wikimedia grant project next year.

Before organizing any events, we wanted to understand what actually stops women in southeast Serbia from contributing online. We conducted a survey with 100 women across the region to map their digital habits and barriers.

The results were revealing:

  • 100% of respondents use the internet every day.
  • 94% act strictly as passive consumers—reading content, but never writing or editing online.
  • Over 86% stated that fear of online attacks, harsh criticism, and judgment from their local, more conservative communities stops them from creating digital content.

title: A Decade of Tulu Wikipedia: Celebrating 10 Years of Community, Culture and Open Knowledge
content:
2008 — Tulu Wikipedia begins as an Incubator project under the Wikimedia Foundation.

2016 — Officially launched as a full Wikipedia project ( 23rd Indian-language Wikipedia) on 6 August 2016 during WikiConference India 2016, Chandigarh.

2026 — Completed a decade of documenting Tulu knowledge on 06 August 2026 in Mangaluru.

From an eight-year journey in the Wikimedia Incubator to a thriving digital knowledge platform with more than 4,000 articles, Tulu Wikipedia’s tenth anniversary celebrated the power of volunteerism, regional collaboration and the preservation of a living language.

In September 2026, the Tulu Wikimedia community came together in Mangaluru, Karnataka, to celebrate a remarkable milestone: ten years of Tulu Wikipedia as a live Wikipedia edition. Held on September 12–13 at A J Grand Hotel, the two-day decennial celebration brought together more than 65 participants, including Wikimedians, students, educators, researchers, language enthusiasts, family members and cultural practitioners.
snippet: 2008 — Tulu Wikipedia begins as an Incubator project under the Wikimedia Foundation.

title: Japan Wikimedia Conference 2026 is coming soon!
content:
The Wikimedians of Japan User Group will hold the Japan Wikimedia Conference 2026 on December 6, 2026, at the Keio University Mita Campus in Tokyo. This conference is intended for those involved in the Wikimedia movement—both in Japan and abroad—as well as those who make use of Wikimedia content.It provides a place for them to connect and share their knowledge and experiences.

Our goal is to bring together a wide range of people — not only Wikipedia contributors, but also contributors to various other Wikimedia projects, those engaged in offline activities such as Wikimedia outreach, those who use Wikimedia project content in their services, and even those who are simply interested in Wikimedia. Through discussion and the exchange of information, we aim to invigorate activities, enable collaboration and mutual support among them, and foster new initiatives.
